board.name: Microsoft Surface Pro 11th Edition (Snapdragon X Elite)

board.note: Model string and compatible of the Surface Pro 11th Edition device tree. This file is a template: board.status stays UNIMPLEMENTED until the X2 probe has measured the values marked UNKNOWN and an operator promotes it.

soc.family.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi (the shared X1E80100 SoC file; the name is the upstream codename)

soc.midr.note: MIDR_EL1 and REVIDR_EL1 are for the X2 probe to measure; a value is not guessed. Lead only: the pinned Linux arch/arm64/include/asm/cputype.h:134 names an Oryon X1 part number, which the measurement should be compared with.

clusters.cores_per_cluster.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:221-275 (cpu-map: core0 to core3 in each cluster)

clusters.mpidr.source: Arm Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile (DDI 0487), MPIDR_EL1 affinity fields; Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:74-213 (cpu reg values differ only in Aff1 and Aff2)
clusters.mpidr.note: The cluster mask is Aff2 because that is the field that separates the three clusters in the device tree.

gic.version.note: hamoa.dtsi:8559 says arm,gic-v3, which does not separate GICv3 from GICv4. The ACPI MADT GICD version field or GICD_PIDR2 measured at X2 decides; an unknown version makes the Hamoa ACPI cross-check refuse.

gic.gicr.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:8561,8568-8569 (size 0x300000 is 12 redistributors of the 0x40000 stride, as the node's GICR * 12 comment says)

timer.frequency_hz.note: The device tree carries no timer frequency (hamoa.dtsi:9114-9121); CNTFRQ_EL0 is measured at X2.

timer.ppi.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:9114-9121 (GIC_PPI 13, 14, 11, 10 as secure physical, physical, virtual, hypervisor; INTID is 16 plus the PPI number per the GIC architecture)

pcie.ecam.note: hamoa.dtsi:3714-3728 describes the PCIe controller by parf/dbi/elbi/atu/config windows, which are not a MCFG allocation. The ACPI MCFG measured at X2 decides.

limits.ipa_bits.note: S2_TXSZ 28u is a 36-bit intermediate physical address space, a property of this monitor rather than of the board. Whether the SP11 PARange covers it is measured at X2.

ranges.dram0.note: The real DRAM map comes from the X2 UEFI memory map.

ranges.gpu-regs.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:4014-4016 (first reg of the gpu node)

ranges.gpu-gmu.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:4173-4175 (first reg of the gmu node)

ranges.mdss-top.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:5553-5555 (the mdss reg, which is only the top-level block, not the whole display engine)

ranges.usb-1-ss0.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:5254-5256 (usb_1_ss0 reg 0x0a600000 size 0xfc100, rounded up to a page multiple for schema v1)
ranges.usb-1-ss0.note: Enabled by Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/x1-microsoft-denali.dtsi:1364-1367 (dr_mode host). The glue block (offset 0xf8800) is inside the window. Not measured on a unit.

ranges.usb-1-ss1.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:5345-5347 (usb_1_ss1 reg 0x0a800000 size 0xfc100, rounded up to a page multiple for schema v1)
ranges.usb-1-ss1.note: Enabled by Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/x1-microsoft-denali.dtsi:1394-1397 (dr_mode host). The glue block (offset 0xf8800) is inside the window. Not measured on a unit.

devices.gpu-gmu.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:4173-4175 (the gmu node carries no disabled status); x1-microsoft-denali.dtsi:769-771 enables the GPU it serves

devices.uart-debug.note: The Denali tree enables uart2 for the embedded controller and uart14 for Bluetooth; neither is shown to be a debug console.

devices.usb-host.source: Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/x1-microsoft-denali.dtsi:1364-1367,1394-1397 (usb_1_ss0 and usb_1_ss1 enabled, dr_mode host); Linux 7475ea8b58616b33c04afb976cf0fbaad9dd63fb arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/hamoa.dtsi:5256,5347
devices.usb-host.note: Two host controllers reach the two Left-side USB-C connectors through PMIC-GLINK (x1-microsoft-denali.dtsi:53-135). Whether either enumerates a Mac gadget is an X3 measurement.

devices.keyboard.note: The pinned Denali tree describes no keyboard transport.

devices.touchpad.note: The pinned Denali tree describes no touchpad transport.

devices.touchscreen.note: The pinned Denali tree describes no touch or pen transport.

devices.wifi.note: A PCIe endpoint named only by its PCI vendor and device id, so no fixed MMIO window is listed. Presence here does not imply that any existing driver applies.

devices.nvme.note: x1-microsoft-denali.dtsi:264-276 and 1015-1022 enable pcie6a with a VREG_NVME_3P3 supply, but no storage endpoint is described.
